title: response_caching plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `response_caching` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component ResponseCachingConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

ResponseCachingConfig.description: Plugin: response_caching — In-memory HTTP response caching. Cache keys are opaque SHA-256 digests over typed, length-framed fields: the effective post-routing destination (proxy, listen path, upstream or direct host/port/scheme, authority, rewritten path), the matched proxy's backend_path, strip_listen_path, and preserve_host_header (so a proxy-only reload that changes the assembled origin path or outbound Host cannot keep replaying the previous route through a retained global instance), the effective frontend scheme from private connection provenance (the proxy regenerates X-Forwarded-Proto from it, so an HTTPS representation is never replayed to plaintext or vice versa), the original authority, method, path, backend-effective outbound query, a mandatory caller-authorization partition (authentication mechanism, resolved identity/consumer, peer SPIFFE identity, and digests of every credential header presented — taken over both the pristine inbound wire header view and the live backend-visible one, so an earlier ai_stream_router credential rewrite cannot erase the original caller distinction; every caller also binds its canonical peer address, and only an anonymous caller's binding is relaxable per anonymous_caller_scope), and a digest of the complete configured/origin-selected Vary tuple including every name, presence flag, and value. Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, and Cookie are mandatory dimensions on every retained response, including anonymous responses, and are emitted in Vary so downstream shared caches cannot cross Ferrum's private caller partition. That Vary list is published on the MISS response itself, and on an honored request Cache-Control: no-cache refresh (X-Cache-Status: BYPASS, which stores its replacement under the same partition), as well as on later hits, so every freshly fetched publicly cacheable response a downstream cache stores already carries the same selection; an origin Vary: * is left untouched. No raw delimiter concatenation is used anywhere in key construction, so an attacker-supplied header or query value cannot forge a field boundary and collide two distinct requests onto one key. Keys are never logged. GET/HEAD lookup requires a private transport-owned proof that the complete H1/H2/H3 upload is empty; non-empty or unproven bodies bypass, and admission rejects deferred request-body transforms that could synthesize bytes after lookup. Honors Cache-Control freshness, upstream Age/Date (a comma-folded repeated Age uses its first member rather than resetting to zero), current Age generation on hits, ETag/Last-Modified revalidation (304, tolerating a bounded number of empty entity-tag list members), Vary, and never caches responses with Set-Cookie (matched case-insensitively, as is Content-Range). Retained entries are sanitized: connection-scoped and proxy-authentication fields (Connection and everything it nominates, Keep-Alive, Proxy-Authenticate, Proxy-Authorization, Proxy-Connection, TE, Trailer, Transfer-Encoding, Upgrade), every field the origin qualified with private="…" or no-cache="…", and every field the shared replay-sanitation policy also applied by ai_semantic_cache and request_deduplication classifies as per-response state (Set-Cookie/Set-Cookie2, WWW-Authenticate, response credentials, per-request trace and correlation identifiers such as traceparent, b3, x-b3-*, X-Request-Id, X-Correlation-Id, Retry-After, and every RateLimit/X-RateLimit/X-AI-RateLimit/Anthropic-RateLimit field) are dropped before storage, so no replay can emit them; the response that produced the miss is delivered untouched. Responses to requests carrying Authorization in either the pristine inbound or live backend-visible view are stored only with an explicit origin shared-cache opt-in (public, must-revalidate, or s-maxage). Partial (206) and validator-only (304) responses, and any response carrying Content-Range, are never stored as reusable representations. Gateway-generated transport failures are refused from typed backend-dispatch provenance on every HTTP version, so listing 502/504 in cacheable_status_codes retains genuine origin error pages without pinning a local connect/read failure over a recovered origin. Includes a bounded FIFO cacheability predictor (amortized O(1) admission, no full-map sort at capacity) that suppresses repeat cache lookups for variants known to be uncacheable. Unsafe-method invalidation is deferred until a non-error origin response (private provenance recorded before after_proxy hooks), is classified independently of cacheable_methods storage eligibility, skips served cache HITs that never contacted the origin, is confined to the same normalized/transformed Host/authority partition as lookup, and treats a slash-terminated mutated path (including the root) as its own descendant boundary so its children are invalidated too. Store-side staging (header delta, reduced snapshot, timing, lookup path, keys) is written only once a request is known to reach the origin (MISS or no-cache refresh), never on a HIT, REVALIDATED, PREDICTED-BYPASS, or request no-store. Lookup outcomes are exported as the bounded ferrum_response_cache_lookups_total{status} counter (hit, miss, bypass, revalidated, predicted_bypass; never a key, path, host, or caller label). Multiple instances on one proxy namespace request staging metadata under response_caching.<instance_id>.* so differing query/consumer/Vary/method/SSE/status policies remain independent across priority order and reload generations. Unknown top-level keys are rejected with path-qualified diagnostics and spelling suggestions so misspelled Vary, consumer, query, Cache-Control, status/method, capacity, or invalidation fields cannot silently weaken isolation or retention. HTTP only.

ttl_seconds.description: Fallback freshness lifetime in seconds when the backend response has no s-maxage, max-age, or Expires, or when respect_cache_control is explicitly false. Must be an unsigned 64-bit integer: a negative value or one above 18446744073709551615 is rejected at admission. With the default true policy, precedence is s-maxage > max-age > Expires minus Date > ttl_seconds; missing Date uses response receipt time. Invalid or repeated Expires, or invalid/repeated Date for Expires-based freshness, means already expired. Upstream Age, Date, response delay, and cache residency still reduce remaining freshness.

max_entries.description: Maximum number of cached entries, 1 to 10000000. Overflow is evicted oldest-first from an insertion-ordered queue in amortized O(1) per admitted entry — no full-map clone or sort is performed while the accounting mutex is held. A value above the ceiling is rejected at admission.

max_entry_size_bytes.description: Maximum size of a single cached response body (1 MiB by default). Larger responses are not cached. Must be greater than zero.

max_total_size_bytes.description: Maximum accounted retained in-memory response-entry footprint across all entries (100 MiB by default). Concurrent stores and replacements are admitted atomically. When the byte cap is the limiting dimension, every expired entry is reclaimed in expiration order through an ordered index; fresh entries are never evicted to admit a new representation, and the store is refused if it still does not fit. Reclamation cost is bounded by entries actually retired rather than by cache size. An entry larger than the cap alone is never cached. Must be greater than zero.

cacheable_methods.description: HTTP methods eligible for caching (uppercased before use, so any letter casing of the two accepted tokens is admitted). Must contain at least one entry, and every entry must be a valid RFC 9110 HTTP method token that is also a bodyless retrieval method — only GET and HEAD are accepted; every other method token, including POST and OPTIONS, is rejected at admission. A body-bearing method is rejected at admission because cache lookup runs in before_proxy, ahead of on_final_request_body, so the exact backend-visible request body cannot be bound into the key. At runtime the transport must observe the complete H1/H2/H3 upload and privately prove it is empty before lookup; a non-empty or unproven body, any Transfer-Encoding, or a non-zero/unparsable Content-Length bypasses lookup and storage.

cacheable_status_codes.description: Response status codes eligible for caching. Must contain at least one entry, and every entry must be a final status between 200 and 599 whose caching semantics the plugin implements. 1xx (interim), 206 (partial content — requires Range/Content-Range, strong-validator, completeness, and request-applicability tracking), 304 (validator metadata that freshens an existing stored representation rather than a representation of its own), and 401/407 (only valid with an authentication challenge that a shared cache cannot retain: WWW-Authenticate is per-response state under the shared replay-sanitation policy and Proxy-Authenticate is hop-scoped, so a stored copy would replay a challenge-less 401/407) are rejected at admission and refused again at store time, so a caller cannot poison the shared cache with a truncated, validator-only, or challenge-less entry. A 2xx response carrying Content-Range is likewise never stored.

respect_cache_control.description: Honor backend Cache-Control directives (no-store, private, no-cache, max-age, s-maxage, must-revalidate, public) and explicit Expires freshness. Setting false ignores the origin's Cache-Control entirely, not only its lifetimes: freshness comes from ttl_seconds instead of Cache-Control and Expires (age accounting still applies), and the origin's storage prohibitions are ignored too — a response marked no-store, private, or no-cache is stored, and fields it qualified with private="…" or no-cache="…" are retained (still only within the mandatory caller partition). Conversely, because public, must-revalidate, and s-maxage are also ignored, a response to an Authorization-bearing request can never satisfy the shared-cache opt-in and is never stored. Parsing is grammar-aware: the qualified field-name forms private="x-account" and no-cache="x-secret" are understood, and the named fields are removed from the retained entry so they are never replayed from the shared cache. A qualified argument that is not a well-formed quoted field-name list (unquoted, unterminated, empty, or not a valid field name) fails closed to the bare directive and the whole response is refused. Duplicate max-age/s-maxage keep the most restrictive value; malformed lifetime directives contribute zero.

respect_no_cache.description: Honor client request Cache-Control. no-cache bypasses lookup and refreshes the entry (the replacement is stored under the same partition and carries the downstream Vary contract); no-store bypasses lookup and stores nothing. A request max-age is enforced against the stored entry's current age, and a request min-fresh against its remaining freshness (RFC 9111 §5.2.1), so an entry the client would not accept is refetched rather than served — a request max-age=0 always refetches. When false, the whole request Cache-Control value is a bound key dimension and none of these directives is acted on.

vary_by_headers.description: Additional request header names (lowercased) to include in the cache key even when the backend does not send Vary. Merged with any backend Vary response header, with the dimensions already published for the base key, and with the mandatory authorization/cookie/proxy-authorization names; the merged list is emitted on the MISS response as well as on later hits. Every entry must be a valid RFC 9110 HTTP field-name token.

ignore_request_headers.description: Operator attestation that these request headers never select the origin's response (for example a per-request X-Request-Id stamped by an upstream CDN or load balancer), so they must not fragment the cache. Each named header is removed from the request in before_proxy, before the cache key is derived, and is therefore never sent to the origin either — the key still binds every header the origin actually receives, so this relaxes hit rate without opening an unbound dimension. Matching is case-insensitive and applies to every request this instance handles. Names are rejected at admission when they are not valid RFC 9110 field-name tokens, when they are also listed in vary_by_headers, when they name a credential or session header (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, the built-in credential headers, or anything the log-redaction rules classify as sensitive), a gateway-owned header the proxy re-asserts on the backend request after lookup (X-Ferrum-Hops and the rest of the X-Ferrum-* namespace, X-Consumer-*, X-Authenticated-Identity, X-Geo-Country, X-Path-Param-*), Host or a hop-by-hop field, Cache-Control, Pragma, Range, Max-Forwards, any If-* precondition, any Content-* field, Expect, Accept, Accept-Encoding, or proxy-owned forwarding identity (any X-Forwarded-* field, Forwarded, X-Real-IP, Via). Family refusals are prefix matches, and these admission refusals are ASCII case-insensitive with _ treated as - (for example, keep_alive, proxy_connection, and transfer_encoding are refused). Stripping a named header and the vary_by_headers overlap check use exact field-name matching (ASCII case-insensitive only), so x_cdn_hop does not remove X-Cdn-Hop. A non-empty list makes this instance a request-header mutator at its priority, so it cannot share a proxy with request_deduplication, which refuses any later header mutator. The operator must also ensure no later plugin derives the response from an ignored header.

anonymous_caller_scope.description: How anonymous callers (no gateway identity, no credential header, no peer SPIFFE identity) are partitioned. The value is trimmed and ASCII-lowercased before it is matched, and caller-address is an accepted alias of caller_address, so caller_address, caller-address, and shared are admitted in any letter casing and with surrounding whitespace. caller_address (default) binds the gateway-resolved canonical peer address, which the origin observes through Ferrum's regenerated X-Forwarded-For; a request whose canonical address cannot be parsed bypasses the cache entirely rather than being keyed incompletely. shared is an explicit operator attestation that the origin does not vary its response by caller address on this route and lets anonymous callers share one retained representation — only set it when that is known-safe, because it re-opens cross-caller replay for address-sensitive origins. It applies to anonymous callers only: an authenticated caller always binds its canonical peer address, because the backend receives Ferrum's regenerated forwarding identity for that caller too and may vary policy or content by it.

add_cache_status_header.description: Add X-Cache-Status (MISS, HIT, BYPASS, REVALIDATED, PREDICTED-BYPASS) to downstream responses. Cache hits also emit a current Age header. Publication of the downstream Vary contract on a MISS or no-cache refresh is independent of this flag.

invalidate_on_unsafe_methods.description: After a non-error origin response (status < 400) to an unsafe method (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, and extension/custom methods, which fail closed as unsafe), invalidate cached entries for the matched path (and descendants under the same path prefix) within the same matched-proxy and normalized/transformed Host/authority partition used by cache lookup. The descendant boundary is the mutated path plus exactly one / separator, so a path that already ends in / — including the root / — is its own boundary and its children are invalidated as well. Invalidation is an indexed exact lookup plus one ordered range over the mutated path's descendants, so its cost is bounded by the entries it removes rather than by cache size. Method safety is independent of cacheable_methods: an unsafe method listed there still invalidates after an origin MISS and non-error response; a served cache HIT that never contacted the origin does not. Safe methods outside cacheable_methods (OPTIONS, or HEAD under a GET-only set) bypass without invalidating. Error responses, transport failures, and gateway-only synthetics do not invalidate. Invalidation uses private origin-status provenance recorded before after_proxy hooks, so an earlier response hook that replaces the client-visible response cannot suppress eviction after a successful mutation.
